questions.question: How many stories of opposition to datacenters did the warehouse count for the United States in the week of 2 November 2026?
questions.answer: The warehouse counted 16 datacenter opposition stories for the United States in the week starting Monday 2 November 2026 (friction_index_weekly, variable opposition_stories, entity attention:datacenters:US, unit count, week labelled 2026-11-02 UTC). The figure is model-extracted: a model classified each news story, and code counted them. The table was last run on 2026-11-06, so the week may have been only partly covered at that point.

questions.question: On the datacenter page's measure, what was the load-weighted real-time price at CAISO's SP15 hub in August 2026, in USD per MWh?
questions.answer: The load-weighted real-time price at CAISO's SP15 hub (TH_SP15_GEN-APND) for August 2026 was 56.9423 USD/MWh (cost_of_power_monthly, derived). That is the hourly real-time price weighted by EIA-930 CAISO demand. The month is complete: 744 real-time hours held out of 744 hours in the month (cost_of_power_monthly). The month is the local August (CAISO, Pacific time). For comparison, the flat-load simple mean was 55.3261 USD/MWh (cost_of_power_monthly).

questions.question: How much electricity did wind generate in ERCOT on 6 November 2026, in MWh?
questions.answer: Not in the warehouse: ERCOT wind generation for 6 November 2026 is not held, so I give no figure. Both tables that carry it have a gap from 5 to 8 November 2026 (UTC dates). The EIA-930 hourly series (eia930_all_generation, entity eia930:ERCO, net_generation_wind_mw) has none of the 24 hours of that local day. ERCOT's daily wind_generation_mwh (ercot_wind_solar_hsl_daily) has no row for 6 November either.

questions.question: What was the highest hourly demand in ERCOT in the week of Monday 2 to Sunday 8 November 2026 (Central time), in MW?
questions.answer: The warehouse holds only part of that week, so I can't give the full-week peak. The highest hourly ERCOT demand among the hours held was 65,888 MW. It occurred at 3 pm Central on 2 November 2026 (eia930_all_demand, entity eia930:ERCO, variable demand_mw, EIA-930, hourly, reported in Central time). Only 72 of the 168 hours in the week are held. Those are all of 2 and 3 November, 18 hours of 4 November and the last 6 hours of 8 November (up to 11 pm Central). Nothing is held from late on 4 November through most of 8 November. The true weekly maximum could therefore be higher if it fell in a missing hour.

questions.question: What was the average hourly day-ahead price at ERCOT's hub average (HB_HUBAVG) in the week of Monday 2 to Sunday 8 November 2026 (Central time), in USD per MWh?
questions.answer: I can only give a partial figure, not the full week's average. The warehouse (iso_dam_hub_prices, variable spp_dam, hourly) holds 120 of the 168 hours for Monday 2 to Sunday 8 November 2026 in Central time. Over those 120 hours, the mean day-ahead price at ERCOT HB_HUBAVG was 39.24 USD/MWh. The held hours run from 12 am Central on 2 November to 11 pm Central on 6 November. The 48 hours of 7 and 8 November are not in the table and nothing was filled in, so 39.24 USD/MWh is the figure for 2 to 6 November only.

questions.question: What was the average hourly nuclear generation in the Lower 48 states in the week of Monday 2 to Sunday 8 November 2026 (UTC), in MW?
questions.answer: The warehouse holds only part of that week, so I can't give a full-week average. eia930_all_generation has Lower 48 (US48) nuclear generation only for Monday 2 to Wednesday 4 November 2026 (UTC). The other 96 hours, 5 to 8 November, are missing. Over the 72 hours held, mean hourly nuclear generation was 79,920.44 MW (eia930_all_generation, US48, net_generation_nuclear_mw, UTC). This figure covers 2 to 4 November only, not the whole week.
